output.reason: A 70-year-old on warfarin with head trauma yesterday now has a bad headache and two episodes of vomiting, features that require immediate emergency imaging and possible anticoagulation reversal for intracranial hemorrhage.
output.patientMessage: Call 911 now. Because you take warfarin and hit your head, a new bad headache with vomiting could mean bleeding around the brain that needs an urgent head CT and possibly reversal of your blood thinner. Do not drive yourself and do not wait for a message reply. If you become drowsy, confused, weak on one side, or have a seizure, tell the dispatcher immediately.
differential: Subdural or other intracranial hemorrhage after head trauma on warfarin

redFlags.quote: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday.
Today I have a bad headache

redFlags.concern: Altered mental status, confusion or drowsiness
Focal weakness, numbness or speech change

output.vitalSigns: No blood pressure, heart rate, temperature or oxygen readings reported; whether any were measured is unknown.

citations.claim: Immediate non-contrast head CT is indicated after head trauma in patients on anticoagulants or over age 65.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis; imaging criteria are clinical knowledge, not a finding about this patient.

citations.claim: Anticoagulated patients with intracranial hemorrhage expand bleeding rapidly, supporting emergency rather than remote assessment.
citations.limitation: Hemorrhage is not confirmed in this patient; reversal management is for the emergency team.
